note: Tsaphonah can mean 'northward' or 'to Zaphon', a town in the Jordan valley in Gad (Josh 13:27); crossing the Jordan from Ephraim to Gilead is eastward, which favours the place name.

Hebrew bene banim is 'sons of sons'; in 1611 'nephew' could mean grandson (Latin nepos), but a modern reader takes it as a sibling's son. Context: grandsons (high confidence). Bene banim is literally 'sons of sons', the normal expression for grandchildren (Gen 45:10; Exod 34:7). The Hebrew is not ambiguous; only the English word 'nephew' has shifted meaning. All major modern translations read 'grandsons'. Other possible meanings: (1) 'nephews' — KJV, using 'nephew' in its older sense 'grandson' (Latin nepos), so no real difference of meaning; (2) 'descendants' more broadly — bene banim can extend to later offspring, though nothing here suggests it.
